name: Yurí
catalog_citation: Goulard, Jean-Pierre & María Emilia Montes Rodríguez. 2013. Los yurí/juri-tikuna en el complejo socio-lingüístico del Noroeste Amazónico. LIAMES 13: 7-65 (open access, UNICAMP OJS; DOI 10.20396/liames.v0i13.1531).
catalog_locator: p. 19, §2.2 h 'Otras prosodias, tonos bajos, oclusión glotal y laringalización' (PDF page 13 of 59, footer 'LIAMES 13.. 19'); file
catalog_quote: h) Otras prosodias, tonos bajos, oclusión glotal y laringalización: No es fácil saber si los actuales tonos del tikuna (sistema en el que hay variantes dialectales importantes) tienen correspondencia con tonos o con acento. La grafía de los autores del vocabulario señala con frecuencia –y en lugares variados- al menos un acento ¿o tono alto? en cada palabra o construcción, pero hay palabras sin diacríticos. Ocasionalmente se marca un acento grave (34) pinà “cerveza y grano de maíz”. En algunos casos podemos postular la hipótesis de que grafías como gh no indican segmentos sino laringalización, vocal postglotal y tonos muy bajos, con casi plena correspondencia a la realización fonética del tikuna hoy (vocales separadas por oclusión glotal, tono descendente muy bajo, laringalizado en la última sílaba ante pausa).

new_statements.translation: h) Other prosodies, low tones, glottal stop and laryngealization: It is not easy to know whether the present-day tones of Tikuna (a system with important dialectal variants) correspond to tones or to accent. The spelling of the authors of the vocabulary frequently marks – and in varying positions – at least one accent (or high tone?) in each word or construction, but there are words without diacritics. Occasionally a grave accent is marked, (34) pinà 'beer and grain of maize'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is recoverable. Yurí is known only from three 19th-century naturalists' wordlists (Martius 1820, Spix 1820, Wallace c.1850; Natterer 1833 ms.). Wallace states that his accent marks show where stress is laid; Carvalho 2009 takes the acute marks in Martius's list as stress marks and notes that Tikuna cognates preserve the Yurí stressed (often final) syllable (wikú > ku, seyú > ʤuʔú); Goulard & Montes 2013 conclude that the marks fall in varying positions, that some words carry none, and that it cannot be decided whether they record stress or high tone (the sister language Tikuna is tonal). Position of word accent therefore variable/lexical in the record, and its nature (stress vs tone) undetermined.
new_statements.exceptions: Words with no diacritic at all; occasional grave accent (pinà); Carvalho 2009: 261 notes that the acute-marked (stressed) syllable is not the one preserved when the first syllable contains a nasal or h (items 9, 10, 15, 18, 24, 25).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms (isolated words, some with possessive prefix tschu-/su-/tcho-) elicited c. 1820-1850 and written in German-, Portuguese- and English-based orthographies; no connected speech, no native-speaker or instrumental data; the analysts (2009, 2013) work from these written forms only.
new_statements.identity_note: Juri = Yurí/Jurí (juri1235), an extinct language of the Içá-Japurá interfluve attested only in wordlists collected 1819-1850 (Martius at Uarivaú on the Japurá; Spix at Fonte Boa from Juri Tocano-Tapuüja transplanted from the Rio Puré; Wallace from Juri migrants on the Rio Negro; Natterer 1833 ms.). Goulard & Montes 2013 treat the three transcriptions as possibly different Yurí dialects. The uncontacted Carabayo (cara1245, ISO cby) of the Rio Puré are argued by Seifart & Echeverri 2014 to speak a Tikuna-Yurí language, possibly a descendant of Yurí; the sister language is Ticuna (ticu1245), which is tonal.

new_statements.quote: The words are spelt with the vowels sounded as in Portuguese, thus, a, e, i, o, u, ai, pronounced ah, a, e, o, oo, i, and the consonants as in English. A tilde, thus ~, over a letter denotes that it has a nasal sound; the accent shows where the stress is to be laid; and a letter placed above the line shows that it is to be very faintly sounded, often in a peculiar way, as the l in walnut.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog carries Yurí with an empty rule; the one existing statement (Goulard & Montes 2013: 19) says it is not easy to know whether the accents in the old Yurí vocabularies correspond to tone or to stress. Wallace's own convention (p. 521) fixes what HIS marks mean (stress), and his fold-out supplies the per-word data: variable position, final most frequent. Compatible with the catalog's uncertainty; adds primary data but no stated rule. Note that Wallace's text is the convention only; the 'reading' is my inference from the marked column, hence low confidence.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Wallace states no rule; he only declares that the acute accent in his tables marks the stressed syllable. Read at face value, the Juri column (98 items, read from the 300-dpi crops) marks stress on most words and the position is not fixed: final in the majority (Tchoncú 'man', Raiuté 'boy', Omohó 'farinha', Rereáh 'wind', Poconé 'arrow', Noiyú 'forest', Nemú 'path', Noinó 'tree', Weramá 'banana', Coinoá 'bark', Tikiriú 'hair', Iyé 'sun', Noimó 'moon', Cowní 'hard', Coanú 'soft', Tuyí 'black', Ahrí 'red', Coetí 'yellow', Paoó 'two', Keuyecopáh 'three', Pañinopúh 'six'), penultimate in a large minority (Tchúre 'woman', Youcóne 'nose', (Tcho)apomórli 'toes', Tíno 'house', Péa 'ground', Aáte 'pig', Wéri 'dog', Oáca 'star', Epóri 'night', Húto 'father', Owúye 'son/daughter', Reréya 'cold', Erímo 'short', Wenóri 'five'), and antepenultimate in a few (Récapu 'bird', Iríneeu 'go download'). Roughly a third of the items, mostly the possessed body-part terms with the (Tcho)- prefix, carry no accent at all.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not marked; one accent per word at most.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Many Juri items are left unaccented (e.g. Uitemi 'girl', (Tcho)kireu 'head', (Tcha)tikou 'teeth', Tura-ch 'belly', Iya 'tobacco', Ii 'fire', Iino 'knife', Noome 'paddle', Rii 'have you water', Tcharicheouki 'I am ill').
new_statements.identity_note: Wallace's Juri list is the Juri of the Solimões 'between the Içá and Japurá', many of whom had migrated to the Rio Negro where Wallace worked (p. 510); Latham (p. 528) places the speakers south of the Japurá. Spix & Martius describe the Juris of the Japurá at Uarivaú and Manacarú (pp. 1221-1237) as one tribe united by language but split into named sub-hordes; a horde called Jauareté-Tapuüja is said to speak a different language (perhaps Uainumá). No dialect distinction is made in either work's linguistic data.

readall_conflicts: No source states a stress rule for Yurí, so there is no direct disagreement, but the sources pull in different directions on how to read the only evidence. Wallace 1853 (p. 521) declares that the acute in his tables 'shows where the stress is to be laid', and his Juri column puts it on the final syllable in most words, on the penult in many and on the antepenult in a few, with about a third of the items unmarked; taken at face value that is non-fixed, lexically variable stress with a final tendency. The existing statement (Goulard & Montes 2013: 19) cautions that for the old Yurí vocabularies it is not easy to know whether such marks correspond to tone or to stress, given that the sister language Tikuna is tonal; Carvalho 2009: 261 (held by the project from the earlier reading) reads the acutes of Martius's list as stress marks. Spix & Martius 1831 is silent on Yurí (its one 'Betonung' remark is about Coeruna). With the language extinct and only 19th-century non-linguist wordlists as primary data, the placement cannot be pinned to a rule.

sources.note: Latin-Juri wordlist collating Martius's own words (Uarivaú, from the principal Miguel, 1820), Spix's (Fonte Boa, Juri Tocano-Tapuüja) and Wallace's (footnote p. 268). Words carry scattered acute marks (e.g. gerühó, pinä, jahü, taöbi). The only convention statement is in the Tupi preface pp. 29-30: the acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' and also separates vowels that do not form a diphthong; no Juri-specific prosodic remark.
